newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour says Tory tax plans to cost 15 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour says Tory tax plans to cost 15 bln stg.

text.p: Britain's Conservative party manifesto contains more than 15 billion pounds of uncosted spending promises, the opposition Labour Party said on Wednesday.
"Today the Tories have made promises without telling us where the money is comimg from, and refuse to rule out extending VAT to new items," Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown said in statement.
Brown said the Conservatives pledge to offer tax breaks to married couples, one of whom does not work and looks after children or invalid relations, would cost between 3.2 and 5.0 billion pounds.
Brown said the Tories new tax plan was looking more and more restricted. "At most it helps 1.9 million people, one in six of couples, and a fraction of tax payers."

Alastair Darling, shadow chief secretary to the Treasury, said Labour had calculated the cost of just some of Tory manifesto proposals and said these alone already totalled 15 billion pounds. Darling said the Conservatives have failed to cost even their flagship policy of tax breaks to some married couples.
"The Conservatives must now come clean. Where is the money coming from?" he said.
